classification.difficultyReason: Combine the alternate segment theorem with the angle at the centre theorem.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Inscribed triangle with a tangent PQ at its upper-right vertex, dashed radii to that vertex and the bottom vertex, centre O, central unknown x and circumference unknown y. Source proportions are schematic.
spec.mathematics: The tangent–chord angle is 78 degrees. The circumference angle y stands on the same arc as central angle x. PQ is tangent at the upper-right vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 78-degree angle and pronumerals appear; supplied answers are omitted.

answer.worked:
By the alternate segment theorem,
$$y=78^\circ.$$
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
$$\begin{align*}x&=2\times78^\circ\\x&=156^\circ.\end{align*}$$
